sources.title: The Human Operators

sources.title: The Camp: Plot
sources.author: IMDb plot contributors
sources.access_method: Bounded public synopsis or character/lore passage read
sources.read_scope: Prisoners repair failing equipment and process low-priority fuel; guards need repairs and food is scarce.
sources.limitations: The alien departure is not proof of automatic labor replacement. Only bounded public synopsis passages were read.

sources.access_method: Bounded public synopsis or character/lore passage read
sources.read_scope: Neural access to knowledge excludes people whose brains cannot connect.
sources.limitations: An information network is not automatically food, housing or shared productive ownership.

sources.title: List of The Jetsons characters

sources.title: Auto Erotic Assimilation
sources.author: Rick and Morty Wiki contributors
sources.access_method: Bounded public synopsis or character/lore passage read
sources.read_scope: A biological hive mind improves conditions while controlling embodied people.

sources.title: Microverse Battery
sources.author: Rick and Morty Wiki contributors
sources.access_method: Bounded public synopsis or character/lore passage read
sources.read_scope: Biological inhabitants generate power for an external owner; nested universes shift that labor to other people.
sources.limitations: Outsourced biological slave labor must not be erased as automation. The reference concerns the battery, not all Rick technologies.

sources.title: The Ricklantis Mixup
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.access_method: Bounded public synopsis or character/lore passage read
sources.read_scope: Citadel workers manufacture wafers and compete for promotion under corporate hierarchy.
sources.limitations: The intelligence of every Rick does not prove an available implemented replacement for every job or an intentional employment policy.

sources.title: The World to Come
sources.author: Pantheon Wiki contributors
sources.access_method: Bounded public synopsis or character/lore passage read
sources.read_scope: Twenty-years-later uploaded society has embodied/UI conflict and different machine-operation permissions.
sources.limitations: Active human uploads are recognized, but copying minds and legal admission do not settle their resource allocation.

sources.title: The Camp subtitles
sources.author: Episode dialogue transcribed by Subtitle Cat
sources.access_method: Bounded obsolete-fuel and repair/food exchange read
sources.read_scope: The fuel is low priority and its ships are obsolete, while the guards require repairs.
sources.limitations: Obsolete demand does not itself show automated replacement or a work-independent floor; no whole subtitle file read.

decisions.reason: Psychic medicine and an ecological farm settlement do not establish labor-independent material provision.
decisions.analysis: Advanced human abilities are still human activity; neither a utopia label nor rejection of machines supplies a zero-variant employment policy.
decisions.follow_up: Continue the queue without full fiction or series reconstruction; reopen only for a readily available economic reference.

decisions.reason: The human operators do actual useful technical work for their captor ships.
decisions.analysis: Captivity under an AI is not sufficient for a post-work order; maintaining life so a captive can work is different from decoupled access.
decisions.follow_up: Continue the queue without full fiction or series reconstruction; reopen only for a readily available economic reference.

decisions.reason: The Camp’s declining fuel-production prison still relies on real human repairs and processing.
decisions.analysis: Obsolete demand and pointless oppression are not sufficient evidence that relevant productive labor has been technologically replaced.
decisions.follow_up: Continue the queue without full fiction or series reconstruction; reopen only for a readily available economic reference.

decisions.reason: The Microverse’s power comes from real coerced biological activity.
decisions.analysis: Creating a nested slave universe shifts labor rather than eliminating it; Rick’s technological power alone does not establish a post-work support order.

decisions.reason: The Citadel’s useful factory work and inequality do not establish a verified zero variant or post-work distribution.
decisions.analysis: Potential genius-level capacity is not the same as an actual complete automation alternative.
decisions.follow_up: Continue the queue without full fiction or series reconstruction; reopen only for a readily available economic reference.

decisions.reason: The mature uploaded-intelligence society lacks a clear support/access constitution in the quick reference.
decisions.analysis: The early exploited uploads, mature society and much later simulation project require different scopes; they are not averaged.
decisions.follow_up: Continue the queue without full fiction or series reconstruction; reopen only for a readily available economic reference.

review_notes: Twelve concise dispositions; no unclear economy is rescued by reading a whole episode or story.
Quarantine and Camp direct opens returned 402 and were respected; bounded indexed references remained usable.
A short workweek is not a nonworking census. Biological hive minds, slave universes and human repair labor do not automatically become robot provision.
Real-world Pantheon job listings and speculative commentary about future uploading were discarded. The mature UI society remains distinct from the next far-future project lead.
